questions.question: What is a half-life $h$ for a nonnegative random variable with survival $S_X(t)$?
options: The variance of the survival function

questions.question: What is the survival function $S_X(t)$?
What does half-life summarize?
options: The probability of two independent events both occurring.
The time by which survival has fallen to half.

questions.question: For exponential decay with rate $\lambda$, what is the half-life?
In exponential waiting models, what distribution summary is half-life?
If a drug concentration decays exponentially, what is its half-life?
options: The time until the concentration is halved

questions.question: Radioactive decay half-life summarizes what?
options: The number of stable atoms initially
The exact time every atom decays

questions.question: If $\lambda=2$, what is the exponential half-life?
If $S_X(5)=1/2$, what can be said about $5$?
What does a shorter half-life indicate?
options: Faster decay or faster event occurrence
Slower decay and later event occurrence
A smaller rate $\lambda$ in the exponential model

questions.question: Why is half-life easy to communicate?
options: The mean lifetime, a familiar everyday average.
The time until every unit has fully decayed.
The rate $\lambda$, the expected number of decays per unit time.
The time until half remains or half have survived.

questions.question: How is half-life related to the median for survival times?
options: The time by which survival has fallen to $1/\mathrm{e}$.
The time by which survival probability is one half.
The mean waiting time, since the median equals the mean.
The time by which the hazard rate has halved.

questions.question: Why is exponential half-life smaller when $\lambda$ is larger?
If $\lambda=0.5$, what is the exponential half-life?
If two exponential decay processes have rates $1$ and $4$, which has shorter half-life?
For an exponential component lifetime, what does the half-life represent?
options: The time all components must fail.
The time by which half of components fail.

questions.question: Why is half-life not necessarily the same as mean lifetime?
options: It is a median-type summary, so it always exceeds the mean
Half-life is half the mean lifetime, so it equals $1/(2\lambda)$
They differ only because the decay is not exactly exponential
It is a median-type summary, while the mean is an average

questions.question: What does the equation $S_X(h)=1/2$ imply about $P(X\le h)$ when $X$ is continuous?
A model has $S_X(3)=0.7$ and $S_X(6)=0.5$. Which time is the half-life?
An exponential waiting time has positive rate $\lambda$. A student uses $1/\lambda$ for its half-life, the time by which half the population remains. Why is this formula incorrect?
options: $1/\lambda$ is the mean, while half-life is $\log(2)/\lambda$
Half-life has no formula for exponentials
